Camera photos: missing GPS, wrong pins or not on the map

Original file has no GPSLocated, but absent from the mapWrong locations and camera clocksPermissions and iCloud

Last updated November 5, 2026

Check original GPS and photo information, then troubleshoot map visibility, camera clocks, permissions and iCloud.

The original file has no GPS: compare it with the import

  1. Keep the camera file and open its information in a photo viewer that shows GPS metadata.
  2. Open the imported image in Apple Photos. On iPhone use Info; on Mac press Command-I.
  3. Compare the filename, capture time and location. Make sure you are checking the same image, rather than a screenshot or a different exported copy.
  4. If neither version has GPS, plan to add a known place or match existing location clues. Repeating the import cannot create missing coordinates.

If the original has GPS but the imported copy does not, investigate the transfer or export path. Try a small original-file transfer and compare the result. If only some photos have locations, examine them individually rather than assigning one diagnosis to the entire card.

Why a phone GPS link may not have helped

Camera-to-phone transfer and location recording are different jobs. A setup can transfer images while location sharing is off, disconnected or unavailable at capture time. Permission settings and the state of the connection are things to check, not proof that a particular brand is unreliable. Features differ by camera, firmware, phone and companion app version.

Use the exact model’s manual to establish whether it records GPS itself, receives it from another device, or supports neither in your configuration. Before another outing, make a short test: connect as instructed, take a photo, then inspect the resulting file. Check the captured file for coordinates; a connection indicator alone is not enough.

Check the camera’s GPS, Bluetooth location-sharing or smartphone-link setting; see the camera manual for instructions.

Add locations afterwards, starting with known places

Once you know whether GPS was absent at capture or lost in transfer, use the camera-photo method guide to choose manual assignment, reference-photo matching, GPX or Apple Health workout routes. For a small group from one place, use the Mac Photos built-in tools. If the photo already has the correct pin, continue with map display checks instead.

Has a location, but does not show on the Photos map

Open the individual photo’s Info panel first. If the pin is correct, browse that area and change the map zoom; nearby photos may be grouped. Do not keep editing a correct location to refresh a view.

Wrong location: check camera clocks and time zones

Compare camera photos and located references at two known moments. Check the date, time zone and clock difference. Split periods if you changed the camera clock during the trip. LensPin previews an offset without changing capture dates and never overwrites an existing location; adjust an already incorrect pin in Photos.

Permissions and iCloud: confirm the same item and library

For new iPhone photos without locations, check Camera location permissions. This cannot add past GPS to imported camera photos. LensPin needs access to the target photos and references; check Photos permissions if expected items are missing. When comparing devices, confirm the same photo and library and allow originals to download and library changes to sync.
